issues.legal_issue: A court setting aside ex parte proceedings may impose reasonable costs and procedural terms, but may not impose terms that are unduly onerous, unclear, place the defendant in a worse position, or effectively decide the disputed merits.
material_facts: The defendants’ counsel had failed to appear because of an accident, and the trial court found good and sufficient cause for the absence.
The defendants sought to reopen the ex parte proceedings and had filed a written statement before the Supreme Court’s interim order.
The trial court made reopening conditional on the defendants depositing monthly lease amounts, although liability for those amounts was disputed.
The High Court set aside that condition as too onerous; the Supreme Court upheld that result, while requiring the defendants to pay costs to obtain the benefit of the orders.
issues.conclusion: The condition requiring deposit of the disputed lease amounts was properly set aside because it was too onerous and also vague and uncertain. Reasonable costs and procedural terms may be imposed; in this case, payment of costs was made a condition of obtaining the benefit of the orders, and the trial was directed to proceed expeditiously.
issues.legal_principle: Order 9 Rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits a court to impose costs or other terms when allowing a defendant to answer a suit after ex parte proceedings. Under Arjun Singh v. Mohinder Kumar, AIR 1964 SC 993, a defendant may participate in later proceedings as of right; an application under Rule 7 is needed to reopen proceedings from the point at which they became ex parte. Terms may address costs and the conduct of further proceedings, and costs should reasonably compensate for loss of time and inconvenience. They must not make the applicant worse off than if no application had been made, effectively decree the suit, pre-judge its merits, or be too onerous.

predicates.application_to_reopen_ex_parte_proceedin: The defendant applied to resume proceedings from the point at which the case had begun to proceed ex parte.
predicates.sufficient_cause_for_absence: The defendant established a sufficient reason for not appearing at the earlier hearing.
predicates.condition_prejudges_disputed_merits: The condition would effectively determine, or require payment of, a matter whose merits remained disputed in the suit.
predicates.condition_is_unduly_burdensome_or_unclea: The condition imposed on reopening would be excessively burdensome or would lack clarity about what compliance required.

issues.definition: When a defendant with sufficient cause seeks to reopen ex parte proceedings, a condition that pre-judges disputed merits or is unduly burdensome or unclear must be set aside.

issues.legal_issue: When possession has been recovered and the defendant waives restitution, the reopened suit may proceed as a claim for accrued monetary relief rather than as a claim for recovery of possession.
material_facts: The plaintiffs obtained possession of the premises during execution of the ex parte decree.
The defendants expressly stated that they would not seek restitution of possession if the ex parte decree was set aside.
The parties had already cross-examined some of the plaintiffs’ witnesses, while other witnesses had not been cross-examined.
The Supreme Court set aside the ex parte proceedings and restored the suit for further trial.
issues.conclusion: The restored suit was to be treated as a claim for recovery of arrears through the date possession was obtained, not as a claim for possession. Witnesses already cross-examined were not to be recalled in light of the defendants’ concession; witnesses not yet cross-examined were to be recalled at the defendants’ cost. The parties could lead further evidence, and the trial was to proceed expeditiously.
issues.legal_principle: The Court tailored the procedure and relief to the subsequent recovery of possession and the defendants’ express waiver of restitution. It restored the monetary dispute for trial, preserved the parties’ opportunity to lead evidence, and gave effect to the defendants’ concession regarding witnesses already cross-examined. No earlier case was relied on for this case-specific direction.

predicates.reopened_civil_suit: A civil suit is restored for trial after an ex parte disposition is set aside.
predicates.possession_recovered_during_proceedings: The claimant obtained possession of the disputed property while the proceedings were ongoing.
predicates.defendant_waives_restitution: The defendant expressly gave up the right to recover possession of the property again.

issues.definition: If a restored civil suit concerns property whose possession the claimant has recovered and the defendant waives restitution, the suit proceeds as a claim for accrued arrears rather than for possession.
